title: Financial Crime Essentials for All Staff
summary: An eight-module foundation programme helping all staff recognise financial crime red flags, follow the firm's controls and report suspicions without tipping off.
intro: This training programme equips all staff in a regulated firm to recognise money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions, bribery and fraud risks in their daily work, and to report concerns promptly without tipping off.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give staff at every level a practical, plain-language understanding of how criminals exploit financial firms and the part each role plays in stopping them. Participants leave able to spot red flags in their own work, follow the firm's controls and report suspicions confidently and lawfully.
sections.What It Covers: How financial crime works, money laundering, terrorist and proliferation financing, customer due diligence, sanctions, bribery and corruption, fraud and scams, and internal reporting, tipping off and red flags across every role.
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including new joiners as part of induction and existing staff as annual refresher training
Customer-facing, operations, payments, technology, HR, finance and procurement staff who may encounter financial crime risk
Line managers who receive concerns from their teams and need to know how to escalate them
Learning Objectives: Explain in plain language how money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions evasion, bribery and fraud work
Recognise the red flags most relevant to their own role and team
Apply the firm's customer due diligence, screening and anti-bribery controls correctly
Identify fraud and scam tactics targeting customers, staff and the firm
Report suspicions internally, promptly and without tipping off
Explain the personal and corporate consequences of financial crime failures and when to speak up
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about ninety minutes each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of short live sessions, and well suited to conversion into e-learning. Modules combine short briefings with real-world examples and scenario questions, work well as annual refresher training, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's policies and business.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of financial crime or regulation is required. Familiarity with the firm's own policies is helpful but not essential.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
OECD (1997), Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions
FATF, Egmont Group and INTERPOL (2023), Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-Enabled Fraud

modules.title: Financial Crime: Why It Matters to Your Job
modules.summary: What financial crime is, why criminals target financial firms, and why every role, not just compliance, forms part of the firm's defences.
objectives: Explain the main types of financial crime and the harm they cause
Describe why firms and staff carry legal obligations to prevent it
Identify where their own role touches financial crime risk
syllabus: The main threats: laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions evasion, bribery and fraud
Real-world harm: victims, communities and the integrity of the financial system
The firm's defences and the role of the money laundering reporting officer
Personal liability, criminal offences and consequences for staff

modules.title: Money Laundering: How Criminal Money Moves
modules.summary: How criminals disguise the proceeds of crime through financial firms, the typologies most often seen in practice, and the warning signs staff should notice.
objectives: Explain placement, layering and integration with practical examples
Recognise common laundering typologies across products and channels
Identify red flags in customer behaviour and transactions
syllabus: The three stages of money laundering in practice
Typologies: cash, money mules, shell companies, trade and digital assets
Professional enablers and the misuse of legitimate businesses
Red flags: unusual activity, unclear source of funds and evasive customers

modules.title: Terrorist Financing and Proliferation Financing
modules.summary: How terrorist and proliferation financing differ from money laundering, why small and legitimate-looking sums matter, and the indicators staff should be aware of.
objectives: Explain how terrorist financing differs from money laundering
Recognise indicators of terrorist and proliferation financing
Describe why small and apparently legitimate transactions can be significant
syllabus: Sources of terrorist finance: legitimate income, crime and abuse of charities
Small sums, crowdfunding and informal value transfer systems
Proliferation financing and dual-use goods in plain terms
Indicators, and why staff should not dismiss low-value concerns

modules.title: Know Your Customer and Customer Due Diligence
modules.summary: Why the firm needs to know who its customers are, what due diligence involves throughout the relationship, and how every team helps keep customer information accurate.
objectives: Explain the purpose of customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring
Recognise higher-risk customers, including politically exposed persons
Apply the firm's procedures when information is missing, inconsistent or suspicious
syllabus: Identification, verification and beneficial ownership
The risk-based approach: simplified, standard and enhanced due diligence
Politically exposed persons, higher-risk countries and complex structures
Ongoing monitoring and keeping customer records up to date

modules.title: Sanctions: What Every Member of Staff Must Know
modules.summary: What financial sanctions prohibit, how the firm screens customers and payments, how evasion happens and why sanctions breaches are treated so seriously.
objectives: Explain asset freezes, trade restrictions and other sanctions measures
Recognise sanctions evasion tactics and screening alerts that need attention
Escalate potential sanctions matches without delay
syllabus: Types of sanctions: asset freezes, sectoral and trade measures
Screening customers, payments and third parties
Evasion red flags: front companies, ownership changes and unusual routing
Why breaches can occur without intent, and what to do on a possible match

modules.title: Bribery and Corruption
modules.summary: How bribery arises in financial services, including through gifts, hospitality, intermediaries and facilitation payments, and the controls that protect staff and the firm.
objectives: Explain what bribery and corruption are and why the firm can be liable
Recognise bribery risks in gifts, hospitality, third parties and procurement
Apply the firm's anti-bribery policy and approval processes
syllabus: Offering, giving, requesting and receiving bribes
Gifts, hospitality, donations and sponsorships: where the line is
Agents, introducers and suppliers: third-party bribery risk
Facilitation payments, public officials and accurate expense records

modules.title: Fraud and Scams: Protecting Customers and the Firm
modules.summary: The fraud and scam tactics aimed at customers, staff and the firm, from impersonation and investment scams to insider fraud, and how staff can intervene before money is lost.
objectives: Recognise common authorised payment, investment and impersonation scams
Identify signs of insider fraud and payment diversion
Intervene appropriately when a customer may be the victim of a scam
syllabus: External fraud: impersonation, investment, romance and invoice scams
Internal fraud, collusion and abuse of system access
Spotting a customer under pressure: conversations that protect them
Deepfakes, synthetic identities and AI-enabled fraud

modules.title: Reporting Suspicion, Tipping Off and Red-Flag Scenarios
modules.summary: How to report a suspicion internally, what happens next, how to avoid tipping off, and a closing set of role-based red-flag scenarios.
objectives: Report suspicions internally through the correct channel and at the right time
Explain tipping off and how to handle customer contact after a report
Apply the programme to realistic scenarios across front office, operations and support roles
syllabus: Internal suspicious activity reports: what to include and when
The money laundering reporting officer, the national FIU and what happens next
Tipping off, prejudicing an investigation and managing customer contact
Workshop: red-flag scenarios by role, what would you do?
